Raw stdout/stderr to EV/gates/.log; then set verdict/exit_code/commit/timestamp(UTC)/log for each gate id in EV/acceptance.json (verdict fields only). base_counts are in EV/state.json baseline.counts (G0 at ba90e71). Hosts: windows/any gates in the packet worktree on Windows. capture gates on the WSL capture host, ONE PLAYWRIGHT INVOCATION AT A TIME across all packets (ports 5173/5174, reuseExistingServer:false): MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -u root -- bash -lc with PATH=/root/.nvm/versions/node/v20.20.2/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin exported first; fetch the needed commits from /mnt/c/Users/Dragonfly/Downloads/Warsha into /root/warsha-visual's object store (NEVER checkout/reset/stash/clean that dirty clone); fresh detached worktree per gate run; pnpm install --frozen-lockfile; port-guard before each run; CI=true; redirect JSON to EV/gates/.json and stderr to .log; detached with .done markers for long runs; never pipe runs through tail; never --update-snapshots. .pw gates: run on a SCRATCH merge of the packet branch onto the CURRENT integration tip (scratch branch/worktree only, never committed to run branches, never pushed); then pw-gate failures vs the named set in the gate command (named/EMPTY.txt for U0/U2/V1, named/H1.txt for H1). Record snapshot writes and dirty-after (must be empty). R1 has no capture gate. Authority rules: do NOT trust $? echo markers inside WSL strings (hook expands them); JSON stats + pw-gate logs are the authority. Read log bodies; classify product vs harness/quoting vs environment before reporting. Never fix anything; failures become repair items returned to the orchestrator. Never edit gates, named sets, snapshots, state.json, PROGRESS.md, DECISIONS.md. Deliverables: all logs, acceptance.json entries, and EV/packets/

/verify.md per packet (per-gate table + uncovered scope + blockers). Final answer UNDER 400 words: per-packet pass/fail table with exit codes and log paths, capture stats per .pw gate (listed/expected/unexpected/outside), and any blocker classified. If a packet's gates cannot run because a sibling holds the ports, wait and retry once; report if still blocked.
